mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over a 3-month window signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 7% triggers a recessionary signal that drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% and UNRATE exceeds 7%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months is associated with a decline in consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and profit pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of three consecutive months of INDPRO declines exceeding 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) and personal savings rate (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a rebuilding phase in the housing market that boosts construction-related equities and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recessionary environment signals an aggressive easing stance that supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS falls below 1% and UNRATE exceeds 7% in a recessionary regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for six consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which raises earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of six consecutive months with monthly PAYEMS increases above 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annual decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 1% for four consecutive quarters signals deflationary pressures that erode corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL YoY change < 1% for 4 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of four consecutive quarters with CPIAUCSL annual declines below 1%.
